newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan port workers to resume night shifts.
newsitem.headline: Japan port workers to resume night shifts.

text.p: Japanese port workers are due to resume night shifts starting on Wednesday after striking for better wages and in protest at U.S. pressure to deregulate Japanese port practices.
"I think night shifts will resume at major ports from 6 p.m.," an official with the Council of Dock Workers' Union of Tokyo said.
Union officials said, however, that port workers would continue to refuse to work on Sundays.
Since March 31, port workers at Japan's main ports, including Yokohama, Osaka, Tokyo, Kobe and Nagoya, had refused to handle freight on the night shift.
Angered by U.S. pressure to deregulate Japanese port practices and hoping to win better working conditions, Japanese port workers held a 24-hour strike on March 12.
The unions next refused to handle freight operations at night.

The U.S. Federal Maritime Commission has said it will impose a $100,000 surcharge on each Japanese vessel entering a U.S. port from abroad beginning on April 14 in retaliation for what it has called unfair Japanese port practices.
Port workers fear that changes sought by the United States could threaten their jobs.
Despite Wednesday's agreement, Japanese port workers and management are still deadlocked over resuming Sunday shifts.
Union members stopped working on Sundays after an agreement regarding Sunday shifts expired on March 9. Management and labour have discussed the issue but have failed to reach an agreement.
An official with a major union said there were no immediate plans to resume Sunday shifts, although management was likely to call for a fresh round of negotiations.
